title: Gifts for 5-Year-Old Girls
headline: Gifts for 5-Year-Old Girls (That Parents Won't Secretly Hate)
seo_title: Best Gifts for 5-Year-Old Girls: 8 Picks Parents Won't Hate | Looks Like Luxe
description: The best gifts for 5-year-old girls, from art easels to Squishmallows to a dreamhouse, curated with sparkle, sarcasm, and zero glitter regrets.
intro: I couldn't help but wonder: when did buying a gift for a five-year-old become a competitive sport?

Because here is the situation. Five is the age where she has opinions, a vocabulary, a very specific favorite color that changes hourly, and absolutely no concept of money. She wants a unicorn. She also wants it to be a mermaid. And the party is Saturday.

So, as your personal gift stylist with a dramatic streak and an Amazon tab problem, I did the research so you don't have to. Eight gifts. Every one has 4.5 stars or higher and hundreds to thousands of reviews at the time I checked. All of them are the kind of present a grown woman could look at and think, honestly, I might want that too.
Pour yourself something chilled. Let's shop.
disclosure: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases, which means if you tap a link and buy, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. Prices and availability live on Amazon.

products.name: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Double-Sided Magnetic Tabletop Easel
products.best_for: The little artist who has already redecorated the fridge
copy: Every girl of five is, in her heart, a visionary. Unfortunately, her canvas of choice is usually your wall.

Enter the tabletop easel: double-sided, magnetic, and designed to give her masterpiece somewhere to live that is not your hallway. Dry-erase on one side, chalk on the other, which means two chances per day to become Picasso.
Verdict: it's the only gift on this list that comes with its own gallery wall.

products.name: Crayola Inspiration Art Case Coloring Set, 140pc
products.best_for: The kid who colors with the intensity of a CEO
copy: Some gifts are trends. Others are classics. A giant case of crayons, markers, and colored pencils is, frankly, the little black dress of childhood.

One hundred forty pieces, crayons and markers and colored pencils, all in one case. It's basically a handbag for people who draw rainbows, and she will carry it with the confidence of a woman heading to a board meeting.
Verdict: unfussy, adored, and impossible to get wrong.

products.name: Squishmallows Official 16" Plush (Anya the Caticorn Mermaid)
products.best_for: The girl who wants a unicorn AND a mermaid AND a cat
copy: Anya is a cat. A unicorn. A mermaid. She is every choice your five-year-old refuses to make, rolled into one extremely huggable marshmallow.
Squishmallows are the plush that inspired actual adult collections, and I say that as someone who has absolutely seen a grown woman defend her shelf of them in public.
Verdict: she'll sleep with it, drag it to dinner, and introduce it to relatives. Plan accordingly.

products.name: Melissa & Doug Disney Sleeping Beauty and Snow White Wooden Dress-Up Dolls
products.best_for: The future stylist who changes outfits five times before breakfast
copy: Fashion is a language, and your five-year-old is fluent. This set gives her two magnetic Disney princesses and 45 clothing magnets, which is roughly the wardrobe budget of a small European monarchy.
It's quiet, tidy, and travels well, which makes it the rare gift that survives restaurants, waiting rooms, and long drives to Grandma's.
Verdict: a closet she can never outgrow and you never have to hang up.

products.name: KidKraft Vintage Wooden Play Kitchen with Pretend Ice Maker and Play Phone
products.best_for: The head chef who will serve you imaginary soup at 7 a.m.
copy: Let's talk about the investment piece. A white wooden kitchen, a little vintage, a little French countryside, and honestly nicer than the one in some of my first apartments.
There's a pretend ice maker and a play phone, so she can run a restaurant and take reservations at the same time. Multitasking is a very grown-up skill, and she's starting early.
Verdict: it looks lovely in a living room, which is exactly what you want from something taking up that much floor.

products.name: Micro Kickboard Mini 3-Wheel Scooter
products.best_for: The girl who has never once walked anywhere
copy: Some girls walk. Some girls skip. Your girl would like to arrive.
A three-wheeled scooter is the grown-up way to give a child freedom, speed, and the quiet confidence of someone who knows they look good in motion. Sidewalk, meet your newest it-girl.
Verdict: pair it with a helmet, a bow, and a bit of swagger, and the whole block will take notes.

products.name: Toniebox 2 Audio Player Starter Set, Cloud Pink
products.best_for: The one who loves bedtime stories and zero screens
copy: Behold, the screen-free gift that parents actually thank you for. A soft pink speaker that plays stories and songs when she places a little character on top. No tablet, no passwords, no negotiations.
It's also pretty enough to sit on a nightstand without making your room look like a toy store, which is a luxury I am prepared to pay extra for.
Verdict: quiet time, finally, with a cloud-colored glow-up.

products.name: Barbie Dreamhouse Dollhouse Playset
products.best_for: The grand gesture. The holiday showstopper. The gift that ends the conversation.
copy: Every list needs a splurge, the way every outfit needs a statement piece. This is it.

Ten play areas, an elevator that is wheelchair accessible, and three custom light settings, because even Barbie believes in mood lighting. It's a full lifestyle in pink, and it's honestly better organized than most of my closets.
Verdict: not the casual birthday-party present, but if you're going for the memory of a lifetime, she will remember this one in therapy, in the best way.

interludes.3: Five is the age where she has opinions, a vocabulary, and no concept of money. Shop accordingly.
interludes.6: A gift is just a tiny love letter that happens to come in a box.

outro: And there you have it: eight gifts, zero glitter regrets (okay, some glitter regrets).

If you take one thing from this guide, let it be this. The best gift for a five-year-old girl is the one that makes her feel seen. Maybe that's a sparkly caticorn. Maybe it's a kitchen with an ice maker. Either way, you're going to be the hero of the party, and you don't have to tell anyone it took you a single evening.
Until the next gift emergency, darling.
